meaning: to remember; to still have in mind; (+ verb) remember to do

senses.en: to remember; to still have something in memory (a person, a name, a fact)
记得 + verb: remember to do something (a friendly reminder)

examples.en: Do you still remember me?
examples.analysis: 记得 is the main verb and 我 its object. 还 'still' before it asks whether the memory has lasted, so this is the line for meeting someone after a long time. 吗 at the end makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: I don't remember his name anymore.
examples.analysis: 不 negates 记得: 不记得 'don't remember'. The final 了 marks a change: you once knew the name and now it is gone. Without 了, 我不记得他的名字 is a plain 'I don't remember his name.'

examples.en: Remember to call Mom.
examples.analysis: Here 记得 is followed by a whole action, 给妈妈打电话 'call Mom', so it means 'remember to do'. With no subject, it is a reminder to the listener, the kind of thing said at the door. 给 + person comes before 打电话.

related.en: to commit to memory, make it stick (记住了 'got it'); 记得 is having it in memory

meaning: to write

senses.en: to write (characters, a name, a message)
to write; to compose (a report, a book, an article)

examples.en: How do you write your name?
examples.analysis: 怎么 + verb asks how something is done: 怎么写 'how is it written'. 你的名字 comes first as the topic, then the question about it. A common question right after a name is said aloud, since many characters share one sound.

examples.en: I can't write Chinese characters.
examples.analysis: 会 + verb = 'know how to'. 不会写 says the skill is missing; a passing obstacle, such as having no pen, would be 写不了 or 不能写. 汉字 'Chinese characters' is the object of 写.

examples.en: Please write your name here.
examples.analysis: A polite request: 请 + 在 + place + verb + object. The place phrase 在这儿 'here' comes before 写, the reverse of English 'write … here'. Typical at a front desk or a clinic.

meaning: to wear; to put on (clothes, shoes)

senses.en: to wear; to have on (clothes, shoes, socks)
to put on (穿上衣服 'put your clothes on')
to cross; to go through (穿马路 'cross the street')

examples.en: It's cold today. Wear an extra layer.
examples.analysis: 多 + verb + 一点儿 = 'do a bit more of it': 多穿一点儿 'wear a bit more', i.e. add a layer. 多 sits before the verb here. 今天很冷 gives the reason first; this is what a parent or partner says on a cold morning.

examples.en: You look good in white.
examples.analysis: 你穿白的 'you wearing white (ones)' is the topic, and 很好看 comments on it. 白的 drops the noun because both sides know it means clothes. English 'look good in' maps onto 穿 + clothes + 好看.

examples.en: There's a meeting tomorrow. What should I wear?
examples.analysis: 穿 + 什么 asks what to put on. The question word sits in the object slot, where the answer will go: 穿白的. 好 at the end, 'what would be good', carries the English 'should'. 明天开会 sets the scene first.

collocations.en: to get dressed; to wear clothes

meaning: where; (哪里哪里) not at all, a modest reply to praise

senses.en: where? (asks for a place)
哪里哪里: oh, not really (a modest reply to a compliment)

examples.en: Where's the restroom?
examples.analysis: 在 + 哪里 = 'is located where'. The question word sits where the answer goes (洗手间在楼上 'it's upstairs'), so the word order does not change as it does in English. No 吗: 哪里 already makes it a question.

examples.en: Where are you from?
examples.analysis: 哪里人 = 'a person of where'. Chinese asks with 是 + 哪里 + 人, and the answer fills the same slot: 我是北京人 'I'm from Beijing'. No verb for 'come from' is needed here; 是 does the work.

examples.zh: 哪里哪里，我还要多学习。
examples.en: Oh, not at all. I still have a lot to learn.
examples.analysis: Doubled, 哪里哪里 is a set, modest reply to praise, roughly 'oh, not really'; it does not ask 'where'. It is a stock polite formula, and in casual talk people also say 没有没有. 还要多学习 'still need to study more' keeps up the modesty.

collocations.en: not at all (a reply to praise)

related.en: where; the same meaning, more common in the north and in casual speech

meaning: to give (as a gift); to deliver; to take or see someone off

senses.en: to give as a present (送你 'it's for you')
to deliver; to bring something to a place
to take, walk or drive someone somewhere; to see a guest off

examples.en: This is a gift for you.
examples.analysis: 送 + person = 'give someone a present'; the receiver follows 送 directly, with no word for 'to'. 我送你的 'what I give you', with 的 standing in for the gift. A typical line when handing over a present.

examples.en: Can you deliver it to my home?
examples.analysis: 送 here means 'deliver'. 送 + 到 + place = 'bring all the way to': 到 marks where the delivery ends. 能…吗 asks whether it can be done, a natural question in a shop after buying something big.

examples.en: No need to see me out, it's cold outside.
examples.analysis: 送 here means walking a guest out. At the door, the guest says 别送了 'no need to see me off': 别 + verb + 了 asks the host not to bother. 外边冷 adds a kind reason.

related.en: to give; any handing over, while 送 is giving as a present
to take; to fetch; to hold

meaning: to run; (casual) to go off somewhere

senses.en: to run
(casual) to go off, take off somewhere (跑哪儿去了 'where did you get to')

examples.en: I ran for an hour. I'm so tired.
examples.analysis: 跑 + 了 + a length of time: 跑了一个小时 'ran for an hour', with the length after the verb and 了. 好累 'so tired': 好 before an adjective works like 'so'.

examples.en: Where did you run off to?
examples.analysis: Here 跑 is not literal running but casual 'go off': 跑 + place + 去 + 了 = 'took off to somewhere'. 哪儿 fills the place slot. A half-annoyed question for someone who has been missing for a while.

examples.en: Run, the bus is coming!
examples.analysis: 快 + verb = 'hurry and…': 快跑 'run, quick!'. 车来了 'the bus is coming', with 了 marking the new situation. 车 is whatever vehicle both people are waiting for; at a bus stop it is the bus.

hook: 跑 has the foot radical 足 on the left; 包 (bāo) on the right hints at the sound.

meaning: month; the moon

senses.en: month: 三个月 'three months'; 五月 'May'
the moon (mostly inside words such as 月亮)

measure.note: 一个月 'one month' (a length); 一月 without 个 is 'January'

examples.en: Which month are you going to Beijing?
examples.analysis: 几月 asks 'which month'. Month names are number + 月 (一月 January … 十二月 December), so the question uses 几 'which number'. The time word goes before the verb 去.

examples.en: He's been in China for three months.
examples.analysis: 三个月 'three months' takes 个 because it is a length of time; without 个, 三月 means 'March'. 来 + place + length + final 了 = 'it has been this long since he arrived, and he is still here'. This frame is for arrival-type verbs like 来 and 到.

examples.en: I won't be home next month.
examples.analysis: 下个月 'next month'; 上个月 is 'last month'. The time phrase opens the sentence, before 我. 不在家 'not at home' here means you will be away, for example on a trip.

hook: 月 began as a drawing of a crescent moon.

meaning: early; (as a greeting) Morning!

senses.en: early (opposite of 晚 'late')
before a verb: early, earlier (早到, 早睡)
早！'Morning!'

examples.en: Morning! Had breakfast yet?
examples.analysis: Said alone, 早 is a short morning greeting, like 'Morning!'; 早上好 is the fuller version. The second 早 belongs to 早饭 'breakfast'. 吃…了吗 asks whether it has happened.

examples.en: It's getting late. Let's go.
examples.analysis: 不早了 is literally 'no longer early': 了 marks the change, so it means 'it's getting late'. It is the stock line for ending a visit or a night out. 我们走吧 'let's go' follows, with 吧 making it a suggestion.

examples.en: Could you come a bit earlier tomorrow?
examples.analysis: Before a verb, 早 means 'early': 早一点儿来 'come a little earlier', with 一点儿 'a bit' between 早 and 来. 好吗 at the end softens the instruction into a request.

meaning: day of the month; number (of a room, a building, a seat)

senses.en: day of the month, in speech: 五号 'the 5th'
number in a series: 三号楼 'Building 3', 八号 'No. 8'

examples.en: What's the date today?
examples.analysis: 几号 asks 'which day of the month'. Speech uses 号 for dates; writing often uses 日 (五月一日 'May 1'). 今天几号 needs no verb; 是 can be added but is often left out.

examples.en: Let's meet on the 15th.
examples.analysis: Number + 号 = 'the …th' of the month. The date goes before the verb: 十五号见面 'meet on the 15th', with no word for 'on'. 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.en: Which room are you in?
examples.analysis: Here 号 numbers things in a series: 几号房间 'room number what'. The answer is a number + 号, such as 308号 'Room 308' (said sān líng bā hào). 住 'stay' covers hotels as well as homes.

related.en: day of the month in written dates

meaning: hour (a length of time)

senses.en: hour, as a length of time: 两个小时 'two hours'

measure.note: 一个小时 'one hour'; 个 is often dropped: 两小时, 半小时

examples.en: I waited an hour for you!
examples.analysis: Verb + 了 + object + length: 等了你一个小时 'waited for you for an hour'. With a person as the object (你), the length comes after it; with an ordinary noun it goes before: 学了两年汉语. Said with feeling, it is a complaint.

examples.zh: 坐飞机去北京要几个小时？
examples.en: How many hours does it take to fly to Beijing?
examples.analysis: 要 + time = 'it takes': 要几个小时 'takes how many hours'. 坐飞机 'by plane' comes before 去北京: the means goes first. 小时 is for lengths of time; clock times use 点 (三点 'three o'clock').

examples.en: I'll be there in half an hour.
examples.analysis: 半个小时 'half an hour': 半 goes before 个小时. For 'an hour and a half', 半 moves after: 一个半小时. 就到 'will be there by then', with 就 stressing that it is soon.

collocations.en: how many hours; a few hours

meaning: important

senses.en: important; that matters

examples.en: What do you think matters most?
examples.analysis: 最 + adjective = 'most': 最重要 'the most important'. 什么 sits in the subject slot, where the answer will go: 身体最重要 'health matters most'. 觉得 'think, feel' asks for an opinion.

examples.en: I've got something important to do, so I'll head off.
examples.analysis: 重要 + 的 + noun: 重要的事 'an important matter'. Two-syllable adjectives usually take 的 before a noun. 先走了 'I'll leave first' is the usual way to excuse yourself early.

examples.en: It doesn't matter. Stop thinking about it.
examples.analysis: 不 negates the adjective directly: 不重要 'not important', with no 是. 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop doing it': 别想了 'stop dwelling on it'. A comforting reply to someone who is worrying.

meaning: other people; someone else

senses.en: other people; someone else (anyone outside the people already in mind)

examples.en: Everyone else has left.
examples.analysis: 别人 'other people' + 都 'all' = 'everyone else'. 都 comes after the subject and before the verb. 走了 'have left'; the speaker, and maybe the listener, are the ones still here.

examples.en: Is this yours or someone else's?
examples.analysis: A 还是 B asks 'A or B?', so no 吗 is needed. 别人的 'someone else's', with 的 standing in for the thing being pointed at, such as a phone left on a table.

examples.en: Don't tell anyone else.
examples.analysis: Two 别s: the first means 'don't', the second is part of 别人 'other people'. 告诉 + person = 'tell someone'. A request to keep something between the two of you.

meaning: man; adult male

senses.en: man; an adult male

examples.en: There's a man at the door asking for you.
examples.analysis: 有 + 个 + noun brings someone new into the story: 'there's a man…'. Casual speech drops the 一 of 一个. 找你 'is looking for you', and 门口 'at the door' sets the place first.

examples.zh: 你觉得他是个好男人吗？
examples.en: Do you think he's a good man?
examples.analysis: 是 + 个 + description: 是个好男人 'is a good man', again with 一 dropped. 好男人 often means a decent, caring man, especially as a partner. 觉得 asks for the listener's opinion.

examples.en: I'm the only man in the house.
examples.analysis: 就 here means 'only': 就我一个男人 'just me, one man'. 家里 'at home, in the household' comes first. 男人 is a grown man; for boys or young men people say 男孩儿 or 男生.

collocations.en: a good man (often as a partner)

hook: 男 is 田 'field' over 力 'strength'; the classic dictionary Shuowen explains it as the one who labors in the fields.

meaning: years old (counts age)

senses.en: year of age: 五岁 'five years old'

examples.en: How old is your son?
examples.analysis: 几岁 asks the age of a child; for adults people ask 多大. Number + 岁 needs no verb. 了 at the end treats the age as a point reached, which is the usual way to ask.

examples.en: I'm thirty-five.
examples.analysis: Age needs no verb here: subject + number + 岁. 今年 'this year' is often added; it anchors the age to now without changing the meaning.

examples.en: My mom is in her sixties.
examples.analysis: Round number + 多 + 岁 = 'sixty-odd': 多 after 六十 means 'and some more'. 我妈妈 has no 的, as usual with family. 了 marks the age as a stage she has reached.

related.en: year; for a length of time (三年 'three years')

meaning: to go out (away from where the speaker is)

senses.en: to go out (of a room, the house)
after a verb: out and away (拿出去 'take it out')

examples.en: I'm just stepping out for a minute.
examples.analysis: 出去 = 'go out', away from where the speaker is now; coming out toward the speaker is 出来. 一下儿 after the verb makes it short and casual: 'for a moment'.

examples.en: It's raining outside. Don't go out.
examples.analysis: 外边下雨了 'it's raining outside (it has started)' gives the reason first; this 了 marks the new situation. 别 + verb + 了 = 'don't, now that things have changed': the rain changes the plan, so 别出去了 'better not go out'.

examples.en: Are we eating out tonight?
examples.analysis: 出去 + another verb = 'go out to do it': 出去吃饭 'go out to eat'. The time word 晚上 opens the question. With no subject, it checks a plan or floats an invitation.

collocations.en: to go out and have fun
to step out for a moment

meaning: to see; to catch sight of

senses.en: to see (the eyes take it in); to catch sight of

examples.en: Have you seen my phone?
examples.analysis: 看见 = 'see' as a result: the phone has come into view. 看 alone is 'look', which says nothing about success. 了吗 asks whether it has happened, and 我的手机 is the object.

examples.en: I didn't see him.
examples.analysis: For an event that did not happen, the negative is 没: 没看见 'didn't see'. 看不见 would mean 'can't see', for example because it is too dark or too far.

examples.zh: 我昨天在商场看见你了。
examples.en: I saw you at the mall yesterday.
examples.analysis: Time and place come before the verb: 昨天 + 在商场 + 看见. English puts them after, 'saw you at the mall yesterday'. 了 at the end marks the sighting as a finished event.

hook: 看 is 手 'hand' over 目 'eye', a hand shading the eyes.

meaning: to make a phone call; to call

senses.en: to make a phone call
给 + person + 打电话: to call someone

examples.en: Call me tonight.
examples.analysis: 给 + person + 打电话 = 'call someone'. The person comes before the verb with 给, unlike English 'call me' (打电话给我 is also heard). With no subject, it is a request to the listener.

examples.en: I called him twice.
examples.analysis: 打电话 can split: 了 and a count go between 打 and 电话. 打了两个电话 'made two calls', with 个 counting the calls. 给他 'to him' comes before the verb.

examples.en: Who called you?
examples.analysis: 谁 'who' is the subject, in the same place as the answer (我妈妈给我打电话了). 了 marks the call as done. A natural question right after someone hangs up.

meaning: to get; to obtain; to receive (often something abstract)

senses.en: to get; to gain; to receive (an answer, knowledge, help, a chance)

examples.zh: 你想从工作中得到什么？
examples.en: What do you want to get out of your work?
examples.analysis: 得到 + 什么 'get what'. 从 + source + 中 = 'out of…': 从工作中 'out of your work'. 想 'want' comes before the verb. For a parcel or a message, people more often say 收到.

examples.zh: 我问了三次，都没得到回答。
examples.en: I asked three times and never got an answer.
examples.analysis: 没 + 得到 = 'didn't get'. 都 'in every case' covers the three times: none of them brought an answer. 问了三次 'asked three times', with the count after the verb.

examples.zh: 多读书，能得到很多知识。
examples.en: Read more and you'll gain a lot of knowledge.
examples.analysis: 得到知识 'gain knowledge': 得到 works well with abstract things. The first part, 多读书 'read more', is the condition; no word for 'if' or 'and' is needed to link it to the result.

meaning: son

senses.en: son

examples.en: This is my son, Xiaoming.
examples.analysis: 这是 + person introduces someone. 我儿子 'my son' needs no 的; close family usually goes straight after the pronoun. The name follows after a pause.

examples.en: Where does your son work?
examples.analysis: 在 + place + 工作 = 'work at': the place phrase comes before the verb, and 哪里 sits in that slot. A common question to parents about a grown-up child.

examples.en: My son started primary school this year.
examples.analysis: 上小学 'go to primary school', with 上 meaning 'attend'. The final 了 marks a new stage: he was not in primary school before. 今年 sets the time before the verb.

meaning: goodbye; see you

senses.en: goodbye; see you (said when parting)
说再见: to say goodbye

examples.en: Well, I'll be off then. Bye!
examples.analysis: 再见 closes the conversation. 先走了 'I'm leaving first' is the usual lead-in when you go before others, and 那 at the start means 'well then'. Casual speech also uses 拜拜 'bye-bye'.

examples.en: Say bye to the teacher.
examples.analysis: 跟 + person + 说 + 再见 = 'say goodbye to someone'; the person comes before 说 with 跟. A parent says this to a child at the school gate.

examples.en: She left without saying goodbye.
examples.analysis: 没 A 就 B = 'did B without doing A first': 没说再见就走了 'left without saying goodbye'. Here 再见 is the thing said, the object of 说.
